The present petition filed under Section 482 Cr.P.C. seeks quashing of FIR No. 465/2013, under Sections 498A/406/34 of the IPC, registered at P.S. Ranhola and all other consequential proceeding emanating therefrom, including the chargesheet pending before the Court of Ms. Aneeza Bishnoi,
learned Metropolitan Magistrate, Mahila Court (West), Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi.

sentences.text: 2. The marriage between petitioner no.1/husband and respondent no.2/wife was solemnized on 09.07.2022.

3. Due to matrimonial differences between petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2, the latter lodged an FIR against the petitioner no. 1 (husband), petitioner no. 2 (father-in-law), petitioner no.
3(mother-in-law) and petitioner no. 4 (brother-in-law).

4. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that during the pendency of the present proceedings, the present matter has been settled and petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2 are residing together in their matrimonial home.

5. Petitioners and complainant/respondent no. 2 are present before the Court and have been duly identified by their respective counsel, as well as the Investigating Officer, A.S.I. Shamsher, P.S.
Ranhola.

sentences.text: The complainant/respondent No.2 states that the matter has been settled with the petitioners and she has been residing with petitioner no. 1 peacefully in their matrimonial home.
She further states that she has no objection if the FIR is quashed and consequent chargesheet are quashed.
7. In view of the settlement between the parties, learned APP for the State also has no objection if the present FIR is quashed.

8. In Gian Singh v. State of Punjab, (2012) 10 SCC 303, the Honble Supreme Court has recognized the need of amicable resolution of disputes by observing as under:-
"61.

entities.text: Gian Singh v. State of Punjab, (2012) 10 SCC 303
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: ... In other words, the High Court must consider whether it would be unfair or contrary to the interest of justice to continue with the criminal proceedings or continuation of criminal proceedings would tantamount to abuse of process of law despite settlement and compromise between the victim and the wrongdoer and whether to secure the ends of justice, it is appropriate that criminal case is put to an end and if the answer to the above question(s) is in the affirmative, the High Court shall be well within its jurisdiction to quash the criminal proceeding."

9. In view of the aforesaid circumstances, and the fact that the parties have put a quietus to the dispute, no useful purpose will be served in continuing with the present FIR No. 465/2013, under Sections 498A/406/34 of the IPC, registered at P.S. Ranhola and all other consequential proceeding emanating therefrom, including the chargesheet pending before the Court of Ms. Aneeza Bishnoi,
learned Metropolitan Magistrate, Mahila Court (West), Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi.
10.

entities.text: Mahila Court (West), Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
In the interest of justice, the petition is allowed, and the FIR No. 465/2013, under Sections 498A/406/34 of the IPC, registered at P.S. Ranhola and all other consequential proceeding emanating therefrom, including the chargesheet pending before the Court of Ms. Aneeza Bishnoi,
learned Metropolitan Magistrate, Mahila Court (West), Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi, is hereby quashed.

12. Pending application(s), if any, also stand disposed of.
